header: (Every function that asks or reads takes the STARTING STATION as a last argument, Durgapur unless given: the Asansol tab's trains have their fares from Asansol (ASN), saved in their own tables.) THE FARE OF A TRAIN FROM DURGAPUR TO THE END OF ITS RUN, read from RailRadar's fare service (GET https://api.railradar.in/v1/trains/{number}/fare?source=DGR&destination=CODE&journeyDate=YYYY-MM-DD&classCode=XX), which relays the railway's own passenger reservation system ("source": "prs" in its reply). It needs the paid plan (the free plan is refused with PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED). Checked on 14 Nov 2026 with about 35 calls:
* ONE CLASS PER CALL. The card asks for the eight reserved classes (CLASSES below) and a class that the train does not have is answered 404 "API:DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE": I simply leave that class out.

* THE DATE MUST BE ONE ON WHICH THE TRAIN IS AT DURGAPUR (a train that runs on Sundays at Durgapur is refused for any other date), so I take the first day from tomorrow on which the train, by its days AT DURGAPUR, runs. Fares did not change between the dates tried (a week and five weeks ahead), so I keep an answer three days.
* NO UNRESERVED FARE and no fare for the local (MEMU) trains: the reservation system holds none (UR, II and the MEMU numbers are all refused). The card says so, and I make up no number.

* The reply itemises the fare: baseFare, reservationCharge, superfastCharge, goodsServiceTax (GST), cateringCharge (Shatabdi, Vande Bharat, Rajdhani...), dynamicFare, tatkalFare, otherCharge, and totalFare. I READ the total and never add it up myself; I only CHECK it against the parts (the total is the parts rounded: up to 4 rupees above their sum, as non-AC totals go up to the next 5 rupees; seen 0 to +4 on 14 Nov 2026) and I refuse an answer that does not add up, or that is not the train asked.
What I ask for is the general quota (GN) and the full adult fare: no concession, no Tatkal, no other quota. A fare is the railway's figure of the day, shown as approximate with that date.

members.name: high

members.name: parts

symbols.name: journeyDateFor
symbols.sig: export function journeyDateFor(days: Day[], now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): string | null
doc: Returns the first day from tomorrow (Indian time) on which a train that is at Durgapur on `days` runs, as "YYYY-MM-DD".

symbols.name: ClassReading
symbols.sig: { kind: "fare"; fare: ClassFare; distance: number; name: string } | { kind: "absent" }

symbols.name: parseClassFare
symbols.sig: export function parseClassFare(status: number, json: unknown, number: string, cls: FareClass): ClassReading
doc: Reads one class's answer. A 404 means the train has no such class. Anything else that is not a clean fare of the train asked is an error: I never guess.

symbols.name: Fetcher
symbols.sig: (url: string) => Promise<{ status: number; json: unknown }>

symbols.name: readClass
symbols.sig: export async function readClass(number: string, to: string, journeyDate: string, cls: FareClass, fetcher: Fetcher, from: string = STATION.code): Promise<ClassReading>
doc: The fares of one train from Durgapur to `to` for the day `journeyDate`: every class asked, the absent ones left out. I ask all eight together (the key's limit is 30 a minute). A rate refusal, a key refusal, a failure of the service or a class whose answer is unreadable makes the whole thing an error, because a half list would be mistaken for the train's real classes. One class of one train from Durgapur to `to`: the reading, or an error for a refusal (429, 401/403), a failure, or an unreadable answer.

symbols.name: askFares
symbols.sig: export async function askFares(number: string, to: string, journeyDate: string, fetcher: Fetcher, from: string = STATION.code): Promise<FareSet>

symbols.name: LOCAL_CLASS
symbols.sig: const LOCAL_CLASS: FareClass = { code: "UR", name: "Unreserved second class (ordinary)" }
doc: THE LOCAL (MEMU) TRAINS: A HINT, NOT A LOOKUP. The reservation system holds no fare for a train with unreserved seats only (its schedule says so: "category": "Local", "isPrsBookable": false), so I WORK OUT the fare of a local train from the railway's own published ordinary-class fare table (src/lib/live/ordinaryFare.ts) for the distance from Durgapur to the end of the run. That distance is the difference of two cumulative distances in RailRadar's schedule of the train (GET /v1/trains/{number}?haltsOnly=true: each stop has "distance" from the start), one request per train. I say it is an estimate, and a range when the distance's own uncertainty crosses a fare step. A train that reverses on the way (cumulative distance not a straight line) gets no hint.

symbols.name: NoHintError
doc: A local train for which no hint can be made (it reverses on its way). This is not a failure of the source, and I remember it so that the next click does not ask again.

symbols.name: parseLocalDistance
symbols.sig: export function parseLocalDistance(json: unknown, number: string, to: string, from: string = STATION.code): number
doc: Gives the distance from Durgapur to `to` along the train's own route, in km, from RailRadar's schedule of the train. I refuse it when the schedule is not that train's, lacks a stop, runs the other way or reverses.

symbols.name: askLocalFare
symbols.sig: export async function askLocalFare(number: string, to: string, fetcher: Fetcher, today: string, from: string = STATION.code): Promise<FareSet>
doc: The hint for a local train: one class, "UR", an estimate from the table; the distance is the rounded km used.

symbols.name: LegFare
doc: THE FARE TO EVERY STOP AFTER DURGAPUR (the "legs"). The plant pays for the fare service for one month, so for each train I collect the fares not only to the end of its run but to EVERY stop after Durgapur: for each class the train has (the classes found for its end station), one request per stop. A class the train does not sell between Durgapur and a stop is simply absent there; a stop for which no class answers has no leg. For a local (MEMU) train the same stops get the table HINT (no request: the distances are in the schedule already read), up to the first reversal on its route (beyond it the cumulative distance is not a line).

members.name: to
doc: The stop's station code and the name RailRadar gives it.

members.name: seq
doc: Its place in the train's route (grows along the run).

members.name: distanceKm
doc: From Durgapur, as the railway gives it (the fare service) or as worked out for a hint.

members.name: durgapurKm
doc: Durgapur's distance from the start of the train's run.

members.name: stops
doc: The halts after Durgapur, in order, each with its distance from Durgapur (km along the route). I cut the list after the first reversal (that stop is kept).

members.name: reverses
doc: True when the train reverses on its way after Durgapur: the stops are those up to it.

symbols.name: parseSchedule
symbols.sig: export function parseSchedule(json: unknown, number: string, from: string = STATION.code): Schedule
doc: Reads the halts after Durgapur from RailRadar's schedule of a train (GET /v1/trains/{number}?haltsOnly=true).

symbols.name: askLeg
symbols.sig: export async function askLeg(number: string, stop: ScheduleStop, classes: FareClass[], date: string, fetcher: Fetcher, from: string = STATION.code): Promise<LegFare | null>
doc: Asks for the fares of the classes `classes` from Durgapur to one stop, one after the other. Returns null when no class answers (the train does not run, or sell, between them).

symbols.name: localLegs
symbols.sig: export function localLegs(schedule: Schedule, today: string): LegFare[]
doc: Makes the hints for a local train's stops after Durgapur (no request): one leg per stop that the table covers.

behaviours: a real Shatabdi chair-car fare is read: total 1005 as the railway gives it, distance 268 km, the parts above zero in print order
the total is the railway's own (1005), not our sum of the rounded parts (1004)
a sleeper fare has no zero parts: basic and reservation only
404 'data not available' means the train has no such class: absent, not an error
an answer for another train, a failure body with 200, a missing total or distance, an unreadable part, or parts that do not add up is refused

a total up to 4 rupees above the sum of its parts is accepted (non-AC totals are rounded UP to the next 5 rupees: parts 101 give 105, 251 give 255, 106 give 110 on 14 Nov 2026), and one rupee below (rounded parts)
the day is the first one from TOMORROW on that the train is at Durgapur: Sunday train on Saturday 14 Nov = 15 Nov; Saturday train = 21 Nov (not today)
a daily train gets tomorrow, and a train with no running day gets none
it is the day in India, not the server's: 11 pm in London on Fri 13 Nov is already Sat 14 Nov in India, so tomorrow is Sunday
the distance from Durgapur to Asansol on 63505 is 106.1 - 63.8 = 42.3 km
a schedule of another train, without Durgapur or the end, running the other way, with a reversal, or with unreadable distances is refused
the hint for Durgapur to Asansol: one class 'UR', an estimate from the table ('table'), Rs 10, 42.3 km, with the two slabs the 2 km tolerance touches (36-40 and 41-45, both Rs 10) and no range
when the distance's uncertainty crosses a fare step the hint is a range with both slabs named: 160.5 km is Rs 35 to 40
a distance beyond the table (500 km) gets no hint: an empty list, not a guess
a local train that reverses gives an EMPTY answer with its name (to be saved, so that it is not asked again), not an error; it has no hint
a refusal (429, 403, 500) or an unreadable schedule is an error, never a hint
only ONE request is made for a local train (its schedule), not eight
the schedule gives the halts after Durgapur with their distance FROM Durgapur, in order, and Durgapur's own distance from the start
a reversal ends the list (its own stop is kept; what follows is not worked out) and says so
a schedule of another train, with no Durgapur, or with an unreadable stop is refused; a stop whose distance goes backwards ends the list
a local train's legs are hints for every stop: Waria 8.7 km Rs 10, Andal 16.9 km Rs 10, Asansol 42.3 km Rs 10, each marked 'table'
a stop's leg holds the classes that answer, with the railway's own distance (43 km, not 42.3), asked one after another: 3 requests for 3 classes
a stop that no class answers (the train does not go, or sell, there) has no leg: null, not an empty leg
a refusal while asking a stop's classes is an error (429, 403)
a mail train with sleeper, 3A, 2A and 1A gets exactly those four, cheapest first, and the classes it lacks are left out
it carries the train, its name, the end station, the day asked for and the distance
it asked each of the eight classes once, from Durgapur, with the day, and the key is nowhere in an address
asked FROM ASANSOL, each class is requested with source=ASN and the set says it is from ASN; asked without it, still Durgapur
a local train's distance is measured from the station given: Durgapur to Asansol on 63505 is 42.3 km, and 'from Asansol to Udl' is refused (it lies before Asansol on this train)
a train with no fare in the reservation system (a local MEMU) gives an empty list, not an error
a rate refusal (429), a key refusal (403, 401) or a failure (500) is an error for the whole set, never a half list
two different distances for one train are refused
the fares are kept three days
